based on the information included in the final monitoring report, there are several procedures 
for data collecting depending on the methodology applicable for each step of the project. The 
organizational structure/26/, along with roles and responsibilities throughout project 
implementation, has been provided in the MR and verified. 
 
PP conducted sampling surveys to gather information needed for the monitoring of Ny,i,j and μy 
parameters. Monitoring surveys/21/22/23/ were conducted across both PIs between June and July 
2024. The minimum sample size of 100 households as per VMR0006 Section 8.4 Option (b) 
were selected to survey for the proportion parameter ny,i,j.and µy. 
 
Sampling captured information on monitoring variables with required confidence/precision 
(90/10 for individual PIs on an annual basis, or 95/10 confidence/precision basis for groups 
of PIs or sampling on a biennial basis). PP has applied 90/10 confidence/precision for 
sampling for each individual project instance. A simple random sampling was used. 
 
The applied confidence interval and precision level is 90/10. The sample size for the 
parameter μy is determined based on the section 8.4 Option (b) of the. VMR0006 methodology, 
i.e. Project target population > 1000: Minimum sample size 100. PP has applied a sample size 
of 101 for K2C, 106 for WB and 105 for VH, both parameters Ny,i,j and μy. The sampling 
approach has been demonstrated in the monitoring survey/21/22/23/ for each PIs. 
 
Relative precision of data is calculated at 8.2% for K2C, 0% for WB and 7% for VH determined 
for the parameter ny,i,j (which is used to calculate parameter Ny,i,j and is less than the precision 
level limit of 10 %.  
 
For parameter μy, calculation of precision level is calculated as 8.1% for K2C, 5.6% for WB and 
7.2% for VH which is used to remove outlier data for average wood fuel consumption for the 
sampled households. Both parameters are derived from survey with sample size accordance 
with the option (b) provided in the section 8.4 of the VMR0006 methodology/7/ which 
compliance with 90/10 confidence precision is not obligatory. 
 
Inconsistencies, such as sampling data variations and data discrepancies, identified between 
the MR, ER, and KPT have been addressed in findings CAR#2, CAR#3, CAR#4, and CAR#5. 
Each of these findings has been thoroughly reviewed and fully resolved to ensure alignment 
and data accuracy across all reports. 
 
The Sampling and surveys for CDM project activities and programmes of activities (Version 
9.0)/31/ states under paragraph 28 that “When the project participants or the 
coordinating/managing entity have applied a sampling approach, the VVB may apply 
acceptance sampling as described in the steps indicated in paragraphs 29–38 below as part of 
validation/verification activities based on an AQL of 1 % and UQL of 15 %, producer risk 10 % 
and consumer risk 10 % which sample size of 25 and acceptance number of 1 is determined. 
The sampled users are taken from each project instance, 9 users from K2C, 8 from WB and 8 
from VH.
